title: How do you calculate break-even volume in one line?
description: Break-even in one line: a quick way to do this case calculation in your head, with a worked example.
hook: Break-even is one of the most common case calculations, and it fits in one line once you see how it works.
body:
The problem

Fixed costs $400k. Price $80, variable cost $60. Break-even volume?

Step by step

  1. $80 − $60 = $20 per unit
  2. Break-even = fixed costs ÷ contribution
  3. $400,000 ÷ $20

Answer: 20,000 units.

How to say it in the interview

Fixed costs are four hundred thousand dollars. Each unit sells for eighty and costs sixty to make. How many units to break even?

First, the profit on each unit: eighty minus sixty is twenty dollars.

Break-even volume is fixed costs divided by that contribution.

Four hundred thousand divided by twenty.

Twenty thousand units.

Then say what it means: can the client realistically sell twenty thousand units?

Notice that the last step is always about meaning. A number on its own earns half the marks; a number with "so what" earns all of them.
